This example uses __memset to fill 257 bytes at offset 1 with 0x5A. memory_check requires every byte in that range to equal 0x5A, while the guard bytes stay 0xCC and the separate source buffer remains untouched. The FILL WORD row must show 257.

The complete program resets two 264-byte buffers before each operation, then checks every source byte, every destination byte and the untouched guard regions. The expected rows are COPY WORD 257, FILL WORD 257, COPY BYTE 255, FILL BYTE 255, COPY16 016, COPY32 032, ZERO CALLS 002 and FAILED 000. WORD/BYTE describe the count width, not the size of each copied item. The numbers are produced by the sample's checks, not return values from these void functions.

The captured screens show black lettering on white for DMG, blue on white for CGB and blue on black for FC. This example verifies RAM operations; the lettering presents the results rather than demonstrating a drawing primitive. Separate emulator checks cover 88 memory cases on each platform, including constant and runtime lengths at 0, 1, 16, 17, 32, 33, 64, 65 and 255 bytes, plus 256 and 257 for the word-count forms. Physical hardware has not been tested.

__memset_small

Fill up to 255 consecutive bytes with one byte value, using an 8-bit count. This is suitable for initializing a small working buffer. Choose __memset when the required length exceeds 255 bytes.

Syntax

c
void __memset_small(void* dst, u8 value, u8 len);

Parameters

dst

Pointer to the first writable destination byte. Reserve enough consecutive bytes for the complete operation; no buffer is allocated for you.

value

The byte repeated at every destination address: 0–255. Use 0 to clear the range. To initialize a u16 array to a nonzero numeric value, assign its elements individually instead.

len

Number of bytes as u8: 0–255. Do not pass 256 to mean a full 256-byte block; that length does not fit this parameter. Use the corresponding function without _small for 256 bytes or more.

Return value

None (void).

Conditions and limits

A zero count transfers no bytes. Side effects in argument expressions still occur: the example calls two pointer-returning functions and observes both calls even though the copy length is zero.

The operation finishes before the caller continues. It neither switches ROM/RAM banks nor clips a range to a buffer boundary. Keep mappings stable, use valid memory ranges and coordinate access with interrupt handlers that use the same buffers.

On GB, these are ordinary CPU memory accesses. They do not wait for safe VRAM/OAM access, start DMA or select a CGB VRAM/WRAM bank. Use the dedicated graphics-transfer APIs for those jobs.

Usage example

c
memory_reset();
__memset_small(memory_destination+1,0x5A,255);
memory_fill_byte=memory_check(255,1);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

This example uses __memset_small to fill 255 bytes at offset 1 with 0x5A. memory_check requires every byte in that range to equal 0x5A, while the guard bytes stay 0xCC and the separate source buffer remains untouched. The FILL BYTE row must show 255.

The complete program resets two 264-byte buffers before each operation, then checks every source byte, every destination byte and the untouched guard regions. The expected rows are COPY WORD 257, FILL WORD 257, COPY BYTE 255, FILL BYTE 255, COPY16 016, COPY32 032, ZERO CALLS 002 and FAILED 000. WORD/BYTE describe the count width, not the size of each copied item. The numbers are produced by the sample's checks, not return values from these void functions.

The captured screens show black lettering on white for DMG, blue on white for CGB and blue on black for FC. This example verifies RAM operations; the lettering presents the results rather than demonstrating a drawing primitive. Separate emulator checks cover 88 memory cases on each platform, including constant and runtime lengths at 0, 1, 16, 17, 32, 33, 64, 65 and 255 bytes, plus 256 and 257 for the word-count forms. Physical hardware has not been tested.

Complete example program

Build command

powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .\out | Out-Null
.\kitaqgb\kitaqgb.exe .\kitaq-docs\samples\api-examples\gb\memory_intrinsics.c -I .\kitaqgb\lib -I .\kitaq-docs\samples -o .\out\memory_intrinsics.gb --profile=dev --rst-disable --stack-bank=fixed --cgb=cgb --no-cache --no-disasm

            // Note: keep the intrinsic name conservative to avoid collisions ("slice" is allowed only
            // when there is no declared function named "slice").
            if (newFunc.Match(Tag.Name, out string __sfname))
            {
                bool isSliceIntrinsic = (__sfname == "__slice") || (__sfname == "slice" && ctx.FindFuncParams("slice") == null);
                if (isSliceIntrinsic)
                {
                    if (newArgs.Length != 2)
                    {
                        Program.Error(expr.Source, ErrorCode.ParseError, "{0}: expected 2 arguments: __slice(ptr,len)", __sfname);
                    }
                    else
                    {
                        CType pty = InferType(ctx, newArgs[0]);
                        if (pty == null || !(pty.IsPointer || pty.IsArray))
                            Program.Error(expr.Source, ErrorCode.ExpectedType, "{0}: first argument must be a pointer or array, got: {1}", __sfname, (pty == null ? "<unknown>" : pty.Show()));

                        CType lty = InferType(ctx, newArgs[1]);
                        if (lty == null || !lty.IsInteger)
                            Program.Error(expr.Source, ErrorCode.ExpectedType, "{0}: second argument must be an integer length, got: {1}", __sfname, (lty == null ? "<unknown>" : lty.Show()));
                    }

                    return Expr.Make(Tag.Slice, newArgs[0], newArgs[1]).WithSource(expr.Source);
                }
            }

            return MakeCall(newFunc, newArgs).WithSource(expr.Source);
        }
__rle_decode_vram

Expand a bank-qualified count/value stream directly into VRAM, without an intermediate output buffer in RAM. The compiler emits a loop that fetches each pair, fills its run using the LCD-aware VRAM write helper, and returns the number of output bytes. This is useful when loading compressed tile data or a byte-oriented tile map.

Syntax

c
u16 __rle_decode_vram(u16 dst, u8 bank, const void* src);

Parameters

dst

16-bit CPU address of the first output byte, within 0x8000–0x9FFF. Reserve enough consecutive bytes without passing 0x9FFF. For example, 0x8860 is tile 134 in the unsigned tile-data layout. The function does not allocate tiles or check the destination range.

bank

Source ROM bank number as u8. The bank and CPU address must match your cartridge mapper and asset placement. Bank selection is restored after each encoded-byte fetch; it is not a destination VRAM-bank selector and cannot express a 9-bit MBC5 bank number.

src

CPU pointer to the encoded stream in the supplied bank. The function increments this address, but keeps the bank number fixed. Keep the full stream, including its terminating zero, inside a readable mapping; crossing 0x7FFF does not automatically continue in the next ROM bank.

Return value

Number of bytes written, as u16. An immediate zero count produces zero bytes and returns 0. The terminator is not copied. Keep the expanded length representable in u16; the return value has no separate error code and is not a tile count.

Conditions and limits

The encoding is byte-oriented, not text-oriented. For example, {3, 0x12, 2, 0xA5, 0} expands to five bytes: 12 12 12 A5 A5. Values are hexadecimal in that output listing. A zero value inside a nonzero-count pair is ordinary data, not the end marker.

There is no encoded-size, output-capacity or malformed-data argument. Validate assets when creating or loading them, provide the zero terminator, and calculate their expanded size before decoding. An invalid or unterminated stream can read past the source and write past the destination.

With the LCD off, runs are written directly. With it on, the helper waits for a writable LCD mode for each output byte, using DI/EI around the wait and store. A long stream can therefore span multiple frames; this is a synchronous call, not a queued transfer. The LCD-on path enables interrupts after each byte instead of preserving an initially disabled interrupt state.

On CGB, writes use the currently selected VBK bank and leave that selection unchanged. Choose VBK 0 for the sample's tile data. The bank argument still selects ROM input, even when VBK 1 is selected for output. The decoder does not manage CGB palettes or map attributes.

Do not let an interrupt routine change the ROM mapping or reuse the far-copy helper while a bank-qualified fetch is in progress. The helpers use shared bank bookkeeping. Place a near decoder and its source in compatible mappings; switching to a function's bank must not hide an ordinary source pointer.

rle_decode and rle_decode_far are declared in rpg.h and implemented in lib/rle.c. Compile that implementation once with your game. The complete example includes rle.c after #pragma bank 0 so that its caller and decoders stay in the common bank; do not also pass rle.c as a separate input for this example. The __rle_decode_vram intrinsic itself needs no library implementation file.

Usage example

c
vram_count=__rle_decode_vram(0x8860,2,banked_rle); // Expand directly to 48 bytes of tile data.
if(*rle_bank_marker!=0xA1)failures++;

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

This example expands the bank-2 stream directly to VRAM at 0x8860, without a RAM output buffer. DIRECT VRAM reads 048. The bottom row is blue on CGB and must contain the same three tile patterns as the RAM-based rows. This teaching program performs the upload with the LCD off.

Each row contains, from left to right, an 8×8 filled square, an 8×8 one-pixel outline, and a filled 4×8 rectangle occupying the left half of an 8×8 tile. Their tile columns are 2, 5 and 8 (pixel x = 16, 40 and 64). The three rows start at pixel y = 32, 72 and 112. DMG uses black shapes; CGB uses red, green and blue by row. FAILED must be 000. The numbers are byte counts: three 16-byte GB tiles require 48 decoded bytes.

The verification matrix checks 42 cases covering an empty stream, a one-byte run, zero-valued data, a 255-byte run, 510-byte output across a destination page, and encoded data across a source page. It compares all 528 observed destination/guard bytes, output length and restored ROM mapping. Direct VRAM cases include LCD on/off on DMG and CGB, plus CGB VBK 1. The two teaching screens are checked after 240 emulator frames. Invalid assets, concurrent interrupt use and physical hardware are not covered.

__rng8

Advance the shared GB pseudorandom generator once and return its new high byte. Use this intrinsic when you need one byte without linking the rng.c library wrappers.

Syntax

c
u8 __rng8();

Return value

One u8 result (0–255), after advancing the shared generator once. This describes the value's type and bounds, not equal likelihood for every byte.

Conditions and limits

The GB step adds 0x5D17 to the 16-bit state with wraparound, XORs the updated low byte with the high byte, then adds that low byte to a one-bit left rotation of the high byte. It stores both updated bytes and returns the high byte.

A zero state is accepted. On the next byte draw, the GB generator substitutes 0x5AA5 before advancing; __rng_seed(0) followed by __rng8() therefore returns 122. Repeatedly reseeding restarts the sequence instead of adding randomness.

These calls share persistent state. Reproduction requires the same target, seed and sequence of calls, including calls made by other helpers. Keep seed and draw operations in one execution context; these checks do not establish safe concurrent use from an interrupt handler.

GB and FC use different algorithms and do not promise the same sequence for the same seed. These are deterministic gameplay generators, not a source of cryptographic randomness; the tests check implementation behavior, not statistical quality or period.

Include rpg.h and compile lib/rng.c alongside your game when using the library functions. The __rng_seed and __rng8 intrinsics themselves are emitted by the compiler; a program using only those two needs no rng.c object.

Usage example

c
__rng_seed(0x1234);
first=__rng8();  // 2: the first draw from this seed on GB.
second=__rng8(); // 34: a second draw advances the same shared state.

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

This sample demonstrates that each draw advances the sequence. After seed 0x1234, the first two __rng8 calls display FIRST 00002 and SECOND 00034. Repeating the seed restarts at 00002.

The complete program prints decimal results on a white background: black text on DMG, blue text on CGB. FAILED must read 00000. The pictures show the actual emulator output of this sample.

Verification compared 32 outputs and eight subsequent byte draws per case with an independent host model: 93 GB cases and 18 FC cases, including constant/runtime seeds and GB range/chance/weight boundaries. The teaching screens were checked after 240 emulator frames. Physical hardware and statistical quality were not tested.

__rng_seed

Replace the shared GB generator's 16-bit state. Use a fixed seed when you want to replay the same sequence during debugging. Seeding itself does not draw a random value.

Syntax

c
void __rng_seed(u16 seed);

Parameters

seed

Unsigned 16-bit seed, 0–65535. Both bytes are stored as supplied. Choose and record the seed before the sequence of gameplay draws you want to reproduce.

Return value

None (void).

Conditions and limits

A zero state is accepted. On the next byte draw, the GB generator substitutes 0x5AA5 before advancing; __rng_seed(0) followed by __rng8() therefore returns 122. Repeatedly reseeding restarts the sequence instead of adding randomness.

These calls share persistent state. Reproduction requires the same target, seed and sequence of calls, including calls made by other helpers. Keep seed and draw operations in one execution context; these checks do not establish safe concurrent use from an interrupt handler.

GB and FC use different algorithms and do not promise the same sequence for the same seed. These are deterministic gameplay generators, not a source of cryptographic randomness; the tests check implementation behavior, not statistical quality or period.

Include rpg.h and compile lib/rng.c alongside your game when using the library functions. The __rng_seed and __rng8 intrinsics themselves are emitted by the compiler; a program using only those two needs no rng.c object.

Usage example

c
__rng_seed(0x1234);
repeated=__rng8(); // Reseeding reproduces the first byte, 2.

__settile_col

Copy len successive tile numbers from src vertically, starting at (x,y) in the LCDC-selected BG map. The source advances one byte and the destination 32 bytes per tile.

Waits for writable VRAM when necessary. The LCD-on path uses interrupt masking and can enable interrupts afterward; it is not a promise to preserve the caller's interrupt state or to finish within one VBlank.

Syntax

c
void __settile_col(u8 x, u8 y, const u8* src, u8 len);

Parameters

x, y

Coordinates in 8×8 tiles, each from 0 to 31. Keep the complete write inside the 32×32 map; coordinates are not clipped.

src

Packed source bytes in RAM or a visible ROM bank. A tile stream contains tile numbers; an attribute stream contains CGB attribute bytes. The routine copies now and does not retain the pointer.

len

Number of bytes, 0–255. Zero copies nothing. Supply at least this many readable source bytes.

Return value

None (void).

Conditions and limits

Tile bytes go to the currently selected VRAM bank. On CGB, select bank 0 for tile numbers; this call does not switch banks for you.

For a horizontal copy keep x+len <= 32; for a vertical copy keep y+len <= 32. The routine does not wrap coordinates at the map edge.

The example uses gb_common.h: m_init() loads the supplied ASCII font with character codes as tile numbers. m_wait(); M_LCDC=0; stops the LCD during VBlank before unsafe transfers. The final LCDC value selects which map is visible.

Usage example

c
// __settile_col
// Copy `len` successive tile numbers from `src` vertically, starting at `(x,y)` in the
// LCDC-selected BG map. The source advances one byte and the destination 32 bytes per
// tile. Waits for writable VRAM when necessary. The LCD-on path uses interrupt masking
// and can enable interrupts afterward; it is not a promise to preserve the caller's
// interrupt state or to finish within one VBlank.
// Expected: FAILED CHECKS 000, with the written tile data in the selected map.
#include "gb_tile_color_example.h"
const u8 example_tiles[] = {'A','B','C'};

void main() {
    u8 failures;
    failures = 0;
    tile_color_example_begin();
    __settile_col(2, 3, example_tiles, 3);
    if (tile_example_read(0x9C62, 0) != 'A') { failures++; }
    if (tile_example_read(0x9CA2, 0) != 'C') { failures++; }
    if (tile_example_read(0x9C63, 0) != 0) { failures++; }
    tile_example_finish(failures, 1);
}

Expected result

The selected map shows the written characters or filled area. The program reads back the addressed tile bytes and, on CGB, the attribute bytes; FAILED CHECKS 000 means those comparisons passed. Both maps initially contain zero, and the example selects 0x9C00 for BG/window before the demonstrated call, so a fixed-map call can be distinguished from a selected-map call. These examples perform the writes with the LCD off; they do not measure LCD-on timing.

On CGB, the sample characters and status text are blue on white. The setup gives palette 0 a blue ink color; it does not change the tile-map attributes. On DMG, the same characters are black on white.

Expected image: the following tile pattern starts at tile coordinates (x=2, y=3), or pixel coordinates (16,24). Each character occupies one 8×8 tile. Read the pattern from top to bottom and left to right; the surrounding tiles remain blank.

text
A

__settile_rect

Fill a w by h rectangle in the LCDC-selected BG map with one tile number. Rows are 32 bytes apart; this repeats a tile, rather than copying an image array.

Waits for writable VRAM when necessary. The LCD-on path uses interrupt masking and can enable interrupts afterward; it is not a promise to preserve the caller's interrupt state or to finish within one VBlank.

Syntax

c
void __settile_rect(u8 x, u8 y, u8 w, u8 h, u8 tile);

Parameters

x, y

Coordinates in 8×8 tiles, each from 0 to 31. Keep the complete write inside the 32×32 map; coordinates are not clipped.

w, h

Width and height in 8×8 tiles. Keep x+w <= 32 and y+h <= 32. A zero dimension performs no write.

tile

Tile number, 0–255. LCDC bit 4 determines how the number addresses tile-image data. It is not a VRAM byte address.

Return value

None (void).

Conditions and limits

Tile bytes go to the currently selected VRAM bank. On CGB, select bank 0 for tile numbers; this call does not switch banks for you.

The example uses gb_common.h: m_init() loads the supplied ASCII font with character codes as tile numbers. m_wait(); M_LCDC=0; stops the LCD during VBlank before unsafe transfers. The final LCDC value selects which map is visible.

Usage example

c
// __settile_rect
// Fill a `w` by `h` rectangle in the LCDC-selected BG map with one tile number. Rows are
// 32 bytes apart; this repeats a tile, rather than copying an image array. Waits for
// writable VRAM when necessary. The LCD-on path uses interrupt masking and can enable
// interrupts afterward; it is not a promise to preserve the caller's interrupt state or
// to finish within one VBlank.
// Expected: FAILED CHECKS 000, with the written tile data in the selected map.
#include "gb_tile_color_example.h"

void main() {
    u8 failures;
    failures = 0;
    tile_color_example_begin();
    __settile_rect(2, 3, 3, 2, 'A');
    if (tile_example_read(0x9C62, 0) != 'A') { failures++; }
    if (tile_example_read(0x9C84, 0) != 'A') { failures++; }
    if (tile_example_read(0x9C65, 0) != 0) { failures++; }
    tile_example_finish(failures, 1);
}

Expected result

The selected map shows the written characters or filled area. The program reads back the addressed tile bytes and, on CGB, the attribute bytes; FAILED CHECKS 000 means those comparisons passed. Both maps initially contain zero, and the example selects 0x9C00 for BG/window before the demonstrated call, so a fixed-map call can be distinguished from a selected-map call. These examples perform the writes with the LCD off; they do not measure LCD-on timing.

On CGB, the sample characters and status text are blue on white. The setup gives palette 0 a blue ink color; it does not change the tile-map attributes. On DMG, the same characters are black on white.

Expected image: the following tile pattern starts at tile coordinates (x=2, y=3), or pixel coordinates (16,24). Each character occupies one 8×8 tile. Read the pattern from top to bottom and left to right; the surrounding tiles remain blank.

__settile_row

Copy len successive tile numbers from src horizontally, starting at (x,y) in the LCDC-selected BG map. Source and destination advance by one byte per tile.

Waits for writable VRAM when necessary. The LCD-on path uses interrupt masking and can enable interrupts afterward; it is not a promise to preserve the caller's interrupt state or to finish within one VBlank.

Parameters

x, y

Coordinates in 8×8 tiles, each from 0 to 31. Keep the complete write inside the 32×32 map; coordinates are not clipped.

src

Packed source bytes in RAM or a visible ROM bank. A tile stream contains tile numbers; an attribute stream contains CGB attribute bytes. The routine copies now and does not retain the pointer.

len

Number of bytes, 0–255. Zero copies nothing. Supply at least this many readable source bytes.

None (void).

Tile bytes go to the currently selected VRAM bank. On CGB, select bank 0 for tile numbers; this call does not switch banks for you.

__vram_copy_dma

__vram_copy_dma is a compiler alias for __vram_memcpy. It uses the same byte-count argument and the same immediate CPU transfer, including its LCD-access rules.

Copy len bytes from src to dst immediately, in increasing address order. The function returns after the copy finishes; it does not enqueue work. Source and destination advance by one byte, without tilemap row strides or tile-format conversion.

Syntax

c
void __vram_copy_dma(u16 dst, const void* src, u16 len);

Parameters

dst

First destination byte address, normally in VRAM 0x8000–0x9FFF. Keep the entire span valid. CGB uses the current VRAM bank; bank 0 contains tile numbers and bank 1 contains map attributes. These routines do not choose a map from LCDC, wrap rows or allocate VRAM.

src

Source byte pointer, valid and mapped for the whole call. Data is read immediately; it is not retained for a later flush. The source bank is not switched automatically. Use non-overlapping spans: this forward copy does not provide memmove semantics.

len

Number of consecutive bytes, 0–65535. It is not a tile count. Keep the complete address range inside valid source and writable destination storage; the API does not check bounds or prevent 16-bit address wrap.

Return value

None (void).

Conditions and limits

The name does not select a DMA engine or schedule work for a later HBlank. The caller waits for completion. With the LCD active, the same CPU polling accepts either mode 0 (HBlank) or mode 1 (VBlank); CGB HDMA is not configured.

With the LCD on, each byte write waits for STAT mode 0 or 1 under DI and is followed by EI. With the LCD off, a plain CPU loop is used. The call can span frames, does not preserve an interrupt-disabled entry state, and does not program DMA registers. Zero length performs no data transfer.

Usage example

c
__vram_copy_dma(0x98A2,strip,3); // This alias also uses CPU writes, not a DMA engine.

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

This example uses __vram_copy_dma to place three map bytes at tile (2,5), pixel (16,40). Expect the three patterns [1,2,3] from left to right in a 24 × 8 area. Neighboring cells must remain blank. The full program places each tested copy or fill on its own row.

The supplied original graphics use tile 1 for a solid 8 × 8 square, tile 2 for its left four columns, and tile 3 for a left-aligned triangle that widens by one pixel per row from 1 to 8 pixels. DMG uses black on white; CGB distinguishes the operations with colors while keeping text black.

The square at pixel (16,88) must remain after zero-length safe and unsafe calls. With the LCD on, safe copy and fill add squares at (16,96) and (32,96). FAILED CHECKS must read 000. The emulator tests compare the drawn pixels as well as the counter. CGB uses bank 0 in this example; other banks and physical hardware are not tested here.

In CGB mode, the operation rows from MEMCPY through FILL UNSAFE cycle through red, blue and green. The ZERO COUNT square is red. In LCD ON, the left square is blue and the right square is green. Text stays black. The checks verify these colors at every drawn pixel.

The emulator tests compare the drawn pixels as well as the counter. CGB uses bank 0 in this example; other banks and physical hardware are not tested here.

In CGB mode, the operation rows from MEMCPY through FILL UNSAFE cycle through red, blue and green. The ZERO COUNT square is red. In LCD ON, the left square is blue and the right square is green. Text stays black. The checks verify these colors at every drawn pixel.

__vram_memset

Immediately fill len consecutive bytes starting at dst with the byte value. This repeats one byte, not a whole tile pattern. A map-byte fill repeats a tile number; a pattern-byte fill instead changes the encoded pixel planes.

Syntax

c
void __vram_memset(u16 dst, u8 value, u16 len);

Parameters

dst

First destination byte address, normally in VRAM 0x8000–0x9FFF. Keep the entire span valid. CGB uses the current VRAM bank; bank 0 contains tile numbers and bank 1 contains map attributes. These routines do not choose a map from LCDC, wrap rows or allocate VRAM.

value

One byte, 0–255, written repeatedly. Its visible meaning depends on whether the destination contains tile indices, pixel planes or another byte-based structure.

len

Number of consecutive bytes, 0–65535. It is not a tile count. Keep the complete address range inside valid source and writable destination storage; the API does not check bounds or prevent 16-bit address wrap.

Return value

None (void).

Conditions and limits

With the LCD on, each byte write waits for STAT mode 0 or 1 under DI and is followed by EI. With the LCD off, a plain CPU loop is used. The call can span frames, does not preserve an interrupt-disabled entry state, and does not program DMA registers. Zero length performs no data transfer.

Usage example

c
__vram_memset(0x98E2,1,length_base+length_extra); // Three solid tiles, not three tile patterns.

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

This example uses __vram_memset to fill three map bytes at tile (2,7), pixel (16,56), with tile number 1. Expect a solid 24 × 8 bar with blank neighboring cells. The count is computed from variables or a function result; all three bytes must still receive value 1.

The supplied original graphics use tile 1 for a solid 8 × 8 square, tile 2 for its left four columns, and tile 3 for a left-aligned triangle that widens by one pixel per row from 1 to 8 pixels. DMG uses black on white; CGB distinguishes the operations with colors while keeping text black.

The square at pixel (16,88) must remain after zero-length safe and unsafe calls. With the LCD on, safe copy and fill add squares at (16,96) and (32,96). FAILED CHECKS must read 000. The emulator tests compare the drawn pixels as well as the counter. CGB uses bank 0 in this example; other banks and physical hardware are not tested here.

In CGB mode, the operation rows from MEMCPY through FILL UNSAFE cycle through red, blue and green. The ZERO COUNT square is red. In LCD ON, the left square is blue and the right square is green. Text stays black. The checks verify these colors at every drawn pixel.

csharp
if (funcName == "__wait_vblank")
            {
                if (args.Length != 0) Error(expr, "__wait_vblank() expects 0 arguments");

                AsmOperand wbRet = MakeUniqueLabel("waitvb_ret");
                AsmOperand wbExitVblank = MakeUniqueLabel("waitvb_exit");
                AsmOperand wbEnterVblank = MakeUniqueLabel("waitvb_enter");

                // If LCD is off, return immediately.
                EmitAsm("LDH_A_MEM", new AsmOperand(0x40, AddressMode.HighMem)); // LCDC
                EmitAsm("AND_IMM", new AsmOperand(0x80, AddressMode.Immediate));
                EmitAsm("JR_Z", wbRet);

                // while (LY >= 144) {}
                EmitLabel(wbExitVblank);
                EmitAsm("LDH_A_MEM", new AsmOperand(0x44, AddressMode.HighMem)); // LY
                EmitAsm("CP_IMM", new AsmOperand(144, AddressMode.Immediate));
                EmitAsm("JR_C", wbEnterVblank);
                EmitAsm("JR", wbExitVblank);

                // while (LY < 144) {}
                EmitLabel(wbEnterVblank);
                EmitAsm("LDH_A_MEM", new AsmOperand(0x44, AddressMode.HighMem)); // LY
                EmitAsm("CP_IMM", new AsmOperand(144, AddressMode.Immediate));
                EmitAsm("JR_C", wbEnterVblank);

                EmitLabel(wbRet);
                return;
            }
__xy_in_rect

Syntax

if (funcName == "__xy_in_rect")
            {
                if (args.Length != 6) Error(expr, "__xy_in_rect(x, y, rx, ry, rw, rh) expects 6 arguments");

                Expr[] foldedRectArgs = args.Select(FoldConstants).ToArray();
                if (foldedRectArgs[0].Match(Tag.Integer, out int constX) &&
                    foldedRectArgs[1].Match(Tag.Integer, out int constY) &&
                    foldedRectArgs[2].Match(Tag.Integer, out int constRx) &&
                    foldedRectArgs[3].Match(Tag.Integer, out int constRy) &&
                    foldedRectArgs[4].Match(Tag.Integer, out int constRw) &&
                    foldedRectArgs[5].Match(Tag.Integer, out int constRh))
                {
                    int x = constX & 0xFF;
                    int y = constY & 0xFF;
                    int rx = constRx & 0xFF;
                    int ry = constRy & 0xFF;
                    int rw = constRw & 0xFF;
                    int rh = constRh & 0xFF;
                    bool inside = x >= rx && y >= ry && (x - rx) < rw && (y - ry) < rh;
                    if (inside) EmitAsm("LD_A_IMM", new AsmOperand(1, AddressMode.Immediate));
                    else EmitAsm("XOR_A");
                    return;
                }

                EmitPushExprAsWord(args[0]); // x
                EmitPushExprAsWord(args[1]); // y
                EmitPushExprAsWord(args[2]); // rx
                EmitPushExprAsWord(args[3]); // ry
                EmitPushExprAsWord(args[4]); // rw
                EmitPushExprAsWord(args[5]); // rh

                AsmOperand ret0 = MakeUniqueLabel("xyrect_ret0");
                AsmOperand done = MakeUniqueLabel("xyrect_done");

                EmitAsm("LD_HL_SP_IMM", new AsmOperand(10, AddressMode.Relative));
                EmitAsm("LD_A_HL");
                EmitAsm("LD_B_A"); // x
                EmitAsm("LD_HL_SP_IMM", new AsmOperand(6, AddressMode.Relative));
                EmitAsm("LD_A_HL");
                EmitAsm("LD_C_A"); // rx
                EmitAsm("LD_A_B");
                EmitAsm("CP_C");
                EmitAsm("JR_C", ret0);
                EmitAsm("SUB_C");
                EmitAsm("LD_B_A");
                EmitAsm("LD_HL_SP_IMM", new AsmOperand(2, AddressMode.Relative));
                EmitAsm("LD_A_HL");
                EmitAsm("LD_C_A"); // rw
                EmitAsm("LD_A_B");
                EmitAsm("CP_C");
                EmitAsm("JR_NC", ret0);

                EmitAsm("LD_HL_SP_IMM", new AsmOperand(8, AddressMode.Relative));
                EmitAsm("LD_A_HL");
                EmitAsm("LD_B_A"); // y
                EmitAsm("LD_HL_SP_IMM", new AsmOperand(4, AddressMode.Relative));
                EmitAsm("LD_A_HL");
                EmitAsm("LD_C_A"); // ry
                EmitAsm("LD_A_B");
                EmitAsm("CP_C");
                EmitAsm("JR_C", ret0);
                EmitAsm("SUB_C");
                EmitAsm("LD_B_A");
                EmitAsm("LD_HL_SP_IMM", new AsmOperand(0, AddressMode.Relative));
                EmitAsm("LD_A_HL");
                EmitAsm("LD_C_A"); // rh
                EmitAsm("LD_A_B");
                EmitAsm("CP_C");
                EmitAsm("JR_NC", ret0);

                EmitAsm("LD_A_IMM", new AsmOperand(1, AddressMode.Immediate));
                EmitAsm("JR", done);
                EmitLabel(ret0);
                EmitAsm("XOR_A");
                EmitLabel(done);
                EmitAsm("ADD_SP_IMM", new AsmOperand(12, AddressMode.Relative));
                return;
            }

scroll.h — Background, window and split scrolling

Control immediate and buffered background/window scrolling and up to eight raster splits. Distinguish getter-managed current values, live hardware registers and pending values.

__scroll_bg_add

Add signed deltas to tracked background coordinates and apply them immediately.

Syntax

c
void __scroll_bg_add(s8 dx, s8 dy);

Parameters

dx

Signed horizontal pixel delta, −128 through 127.

dy

Signed vertical pixel delta, −128 through 127.

Return value

No return value. The affected state and when it takes effect are described in this entry.

Conditions and limits

No wait is performed. Immediate setters/additions synchronize the affected pending pair to current values and clear its dirty flag. Even a single-axis immediate setter cancels the other pending axis in the same pair. Results wrap modulo 256. Additions start from tracked current values, not pending values or temporary raster register values.

Usage example

c
__scroll_bg_add(-20,3);result[22]=M_SCX;result[23]=M_SCY;

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Learn immediate versus pending values and wrapping signed additions. BG X is 250 before flush and 16 afterward; WX changes from 23 to 39. Adding −20 to BG X produces 252; adding −40 to WY produces 248. The visual example also shows a background rectangle and an independent window frame.

Complete example program

Camera_Set(&view,2048,4096);
Camera_ApplyBg(&view);

Expected result

                EmitStoreA(ScrollDirtyVar);
                return;

if (funcName == "__scroll_flush")
            {
                if (args.Length != 0) Error(expr, "__scroll_flush() expects 0 arguments");
                EnsureScrollState();

                AsmOperand flushSkipBg = MakeUniqueLabel("scroll_flush_skip_bg");
                AsmOperand flushSkipWin = MakeUniqueLabel("scroll_flush_skip_win");

                EmitLoadA(ScrollDirtyVar);
                EmitAsm("AND_IMM", new AsmOperand(ScrollDirtyBgMask, AddressMode.Immediate));
                EmitAsm("JR_Z", flushSkipBg);
                EmitLoadA(ScrollBgXNextVar);
                EmitStoreA(ScrollBgXCurVar);
                EmitAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x43, AddressMode.HighMem)); // SCX
                EmitLoadA(ScrollBgYNextVar);
                EmitStoreA(ScrollBgYCurVar);
                EmitAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x42, AddressMode.HighMem)); // SCY
                EmitLabel(flushSkipBg);

                EmitLoadA(ScrollDirtyVar);
                EmitAsm("AND_IMM", new AsmOperand(ScrollDirtyWinMask, AddressMode.Immediate));
                EmitAsm("JR_Z", flushSkipWin);
                EmitLoadA(ScrollWinXNextVar);
                EmitStoreA(ScrollWinXCurVar);
                EmitAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x4B, AddressMode.HighMem)); // WX
                EmitLoadA(ScrollWinYNextVar);
                EmitStoreA(ScrollWinYCurVar);
                EmitAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x4A, AddressMode.HighMem)); // WY
                EmitLabel(flushSkipWin);

                EmitAsm("XOR_A");
                EmitStoreA(ScrollDirtyVar);
                return;
            }
__scroll_split_commit

Capture base window visibility and arm the first scanline event in the split table.

Syntax

c
void __scroll_split_commit();

Return value

No return value. The affected state and when it takes effect are described in this entry.

Conditions and limits

The shared table holds eight entries. Appending neither applies nor sorts them, and excess entries are ignored. Rebuild with reset→push→commit at a safe frame boundary and space events far enough apart for the handler to finish. Interrupt latency means the scheduled line and first affected pixel need not coincide. A nonempty table enables VBlank/STAT in IE and executes EI. An empty table disables the LYC source but does not restore IE or CPU interrupt state.

Usage example

c
__scroll_split_commit();

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Split the screen into three scrolling bands with BG X=0→8→16. Three 24×16 rectangles appear at screen (32,16), (24,80) and (16,112). Events are scheduled at LY=64 and 104. Rectangles are black on DMG and red on CGB.

            {

                UseScrollSplitHelpers = true;
                EmitAsm("CALL", new AsmOperand("__kq_scroll_split_commit_core", AddressMode.Absolute));
                return;

void AppendScrollHelpersIfUsed(List<Expr> rawLines)
    {
        bool needScrollHelpers = UseScrollSplitHelpers;
        if (!needScrollHelpers)
        {
            foreach (var e in rawLines)
            {
                string m;
                AsmOperand o;
                if (!e.Match(Tag.Asm, out m, out o) || o == null || !o.Base.HasValue) continue;
                string target = o.Base.Value;
                if (target == "__kq_scroll_split_reset_core" ||
                    target == "__kq_scroll_split_push_core" ||
                    target == "__kq_scroll_split_commit_core")
                {
                    needScrollHelpers = true;
                    break;
                }
            }
        }

        if (!needScrollHelpers) return;

        EnsureScrollState();

        var injected = new List<Expr>();
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Comment, "[KITAQGB] injected scroll split helpers"));

        // Reset the split count/index and disable STAT coincidence interrupts; existing table bytes are left in place.
        string resetDone = "__kq_scroll_split_reset_done";
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Function, "__kq_scroll_split_reset_core"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("XOR_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_MEM_A", ScrollSplitCountVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_MEM_A", ScrollSplitEnabledVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_MEM_A", ScrollSplitIndexVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_A_MEM", new AsmOperand(0x41, AddressMode.HighMem))); // STAT
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("AND_IMM", new AsmOperand(0xBF, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x41, AddressMode.HighMem)));
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Label, resetDone));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("RET"));

        // Append staged LY, SCX, SCY, WX, WY and masked flags; silently ignore entries beyond the eight-slot capacity.
        string pushHaveRoom = "__kq_scroll_split_push_have_room";
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Function, "__kq_scroll_split_push_core"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", ScrollSplitCountVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("CP_IMM", new AsmOperand(ScrollSplitMaxEntries, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("JR_C", new AsmOperand(pushHaveRoom, AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("RET"));
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Label, pushHaveRoom));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_E_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_D_IMM", new AsmOperand(0, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_L_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_H_IMM", new AsmOperand(0, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("ADD_HL_HL"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("ADD_HL_DE"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("ADD_HL_HL"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_DE_IMM", new AsmOperand(ScrollSplitTableAddr, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("ADD_HL_DE"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", ScrollSplitTmpLyVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDI_HL_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", ScrollSplitTmpScxVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDI_HL_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", ScrollSplitTmpScyVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDI_HL_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", ScrollSplitTmpWxVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDI_HL_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", ScrollSplitTmpWyVar));

        // Schedule entry A by programming LYC and STAT bit 6, or disable that bit when A is outside the current count.

        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_A_MEM", new AsmOperand(0x41, AddressMode.HighMem))); // STAT
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("OR_IMM", new AsmOperand(0x40, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x41, AddressMode.HighMem)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("RET"));

        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Label, statDisable));

        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_A_MEM", new AsmOperand(0x41, AddressMode.HighMem)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("AND_IMM", new AsmOperand(0x40, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("JR_Z", new AsmOperand(statDone, AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_A_MEM", new AsmOperand(0x41, AddressMode.HighMem))); // STAT
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("AND_IMM", new AsmOperand(0xBF, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x41, AddressMode.HighMem)));
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Label, statDone));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("POP_AF"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x70, AddressMode.HighMem))); // restore SVBK
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("POP_HL"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("POP_DE"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("POP_BC"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("POP_AF"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("RETI"));

        int insertAt = 0;
        while (insertAt < rawLines.Count && rawLines[insertAt].MatchTag(Tag.RstMap)) insertAt++;
        rawLines.InsertRange(insertAt, injected);
    }
__scroll_split_push

Append a split entry that changes background scrolling at the requested scanline event.

Syntax

c
void __scroll_split_push(u8 ly, u8 scx, u8 scy);

Parameters

ly

Scanline event number; use 0–143 for visible events and append in ascending order. A first entry at zero is applied during VBlank.

scx

Horizontal background scroll, 0–255 pixels; increasing it moves the background left.

scy

Vertical background scroll, 0–255 pixels; increasing it moves the background up.

Return value

No return value. The affected state and when it takes effect are described in this entry.

Conditions and limits

The shared table holds eight entries. Appending neither applies nor sorts them, and excess entries are ignored. Rebuild with reset→push→commit at a safe frame boundary and space events far enough apart for the handler to finish. Interrupt latency means the scheduled line and first affected pixel need not coincide.

Usage example

c
__scroll_split_push(64,8,0);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Split the screen into three scrolling bands with BG X=0→8→16. Three 24×16 rectangles appear at screen (32,16), (24,80) and (16,112). Events are scheduled at LY=64 and 104. Rectangles are black on DMG and red on CGB.

Complete example program

Build command

powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .\out | Out-Null
.\kitaqgb\kitaqgb.exe .\kitaq-docs\samples\api-examples\gb\batch2_split_intrinsics.c -I .\kitaqgb\lib -I .\kitaq-docs\samples -o .\out\batch2_split_intrinsics.gb --no-cache --no-disasm --profile=dev --rst-disable --stack-bank=fixed --cgb=cgb --cart=mbc5 --romsize=64k

void AppendScrollHelpersIfUsed(List<Expr> rawLines)
    {
        bool needScrollHelpers = UseScrollSplitHelpers;
        if (!needScrollHelpers)
        {
            foreach (var e in rawLines)
            {
                string m;
                AsmOperand o;
                if (!e.Match(Tag.Asm, out m, out o) || o == null || !o.Base.HasValue) continue;
                string target = o.Base.Value;
                if (target == "__kq_scroll_split_reset_core" ||
                    target == "__kq_scroll_split_push_core" ||
                    target == "__kq_scroll_split_commit_core")
                {
                    needScrollHelpers = true;
                    break;
                }
            }
        }

        if (!needScrollHelpers) return;

        EnsureScrollState();

        var injected = new List<Expr>();
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Comment, "[KITAQGB] injected scroll split helpers"));

        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x41, AddressMode.HighMem)));
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Label, resetDone));

        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_DE_IMM", new AsmOperand(ScrollSplitTableAddr, AddressMode.Immediate)));

        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", ScrollSplitTmpLyVar));

        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDI_HL_A"));

        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", ScrollSplitTmpWxVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDI_HL_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", ScrollSplitTmpWyVar));

        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", ScrollSplitTmpFlagsVar));

        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Label, schedHaveTarget));

        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_D_IMM", new AsmOperand(0, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_L_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_H_IMM", new AsmOperand(0, AddressMode.Immediate)));

        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x41, AddressMode.HighMem)));

        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("JR_NZ", new AsmOperand(statDone, AddressMode.Absolute)));

        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("INC_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_MEM_A", ScrollSplitIndexVar));

        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Label, statDisable));
        // Acknowledge an already-disabled source without writing STAT again.
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_A_MEM", new AsmOperand(0x41, AddressMode.HighMem)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("AND_IMM", new AsmOperand(0x40, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("JR_Z", new AsmOperand(statDone, AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_A_MEM", new AsmOperand(0x41, AddressMode.HighMem))); // STAT
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("AND_IMM", new AsmOperand(0xBF, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x41, AddressMode.HighMem)));
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Label, statDone));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("POP_AF"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x70, AddressMode.HighMem))); // restore SVBK
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("POP_HL"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("POP_DE"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("POP_BC"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("POP_AF"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("RETI"));

        int insertAt = 0;
        while (insertAt < rawLines.Count && rawLines[insertAt].MatchTag(Tag.RstMap)) insertAt++;
        rawLines.InsertRange(insertAt, injected);
    }
__scroll_split_push_ex

Append a split entry whose flags select background, window, visibility or background-color-zero operations.

Syntax

c
void __scroll_split_push_ex(u8 ly, u8 scx, u8 scy, u8 wx, u8 wy, u8 flags);

Parameters

ly

Scanline event number; use 0–143 for visible events and append in ascending order. A first entry at zero is applied during VBlank.

scx

Horizontal background scroll, 0–255 pixels; increasing it moves the background left.

scy

Vertical background scroll, 0–255 pixels; increasing it moves the background up.

wx

Raw WX byte, 0–255: add 7 to the desired screen X; the left edge uses 7.

wy

Window top in screen Y pixels, 0–255; visible rows are 0–143.

flags

Operation bits: BG=1, window position=2, show=4, hide=8, CGB background palette 0/color 0=16. Unknown bits are discarded. Color-zero mode reuses scx/scy for the RGB15 low/high bytes.

Return value

No return value. The affected state and when it takes effect are described in this entry.

Conditions and limits

The shared table holds eight entries. Appending neither applies nor sorts them, and excess entries are ignored. Rebuild with reset→push→commit at a safe frame boundary and space events far enough apart for the handler to finish. Interrupt latency means the scheduled line and first affected pixel need not coincide. Show wins when both visibility bits are set. Color zero is CGB-only; combining it with BG movement uses the same scx/scy bytes for both purposes.

Usage example

c
__scroll_split_push_ex(104,16,0,7,0,KQ_SCROLL_SPLIT_USE_BG|KQ_SCROLL_SPLIT_WIN_HIDE);

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Split the screen into three scrolling bands with BG X=0→8→16. Three 24×16 rectangles appear at screen (32,16), (24,80) and (16,112). Events are scheduled at LY=64 and 104. Rectangles are black on DMG and red on CGB.

Complete example program

powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .\out | Out-Null
.\kitaqgb\kitaqgb.exe .\kitaq-docs\samples\api-examples\gb\batch2_split_intrinsics.c -I .\kitaqgb\lib -I .\kitaq-docs\samples -o .\out\batch2_split_intrinsics.gb --no-cache --no-disasm --profile=dev --rst-disable --stack-bank=fixed --cgb=cgb --cart=mbc5 --romsize=64k

void AppendScrollHelpersIfUsed(List<Expr> rawLines)
    {
        bool needScrollHelpers = UseScrollSplitHelpers;
        if (!needScrollHelpers)
        {
            foreach (var e in rawLines)
            {
                string m;
                AsmOperand o;
                if (!e.Match(Tag.Asm, out m, out o) || o == null || !o.Base.HasValue) continue;
                string target = o.Base.Value;
                if (target == "__kq_scroll_split_reset_core" ||
                    target == "__kq_scroll_split_push_core" ||
                    target == "__kq_scroll_split_commit_core")
                {
                    needScrollHelpers = true;
                    break;
                }
            }
        }

        if (!needScrollHelpers) return;

        EnsureScrollState();

        var injected = new List<Expr>();
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Comment, "[KITAQGB] injected scroll split helpers"));

        // Reset the split count/index and disable STAT coincidence interrupts; existing table bytes are left in place.
        string resetDone = "__kq_scroll_split_reset_done";
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Function, "__kq_scroll_split_reset_core"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("XOR_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_MEM_A", ScrollSplitCountVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_MEM_A", ScrollSplitEnabledVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_MEM_A", ScrollSplitIndexVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_A_MEM", new AsmOperand(0x41, AddressMode.HighMem))); // STAT
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("AND_IMM", new AsmOperand(0xBF, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x41, AddressMode.HighMem)));
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Label, resetDone));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("RET"));

        // Append staged LY, SCX, SCY, WX, WY and masked flags; silently ignore entries beyond the eight-slot capacity.
        string pushHaveRoom = "__kq_scroll_split_push_have_room";
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Function, "__kq_scroll_split_push_core"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", ScrollSplitCountVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("CP_IMM", new AsmOperand(ScrollSplitMaxEntries, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("JR_C", new AsmOperand(pushHaveRoom, AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("RET"));

__scroll_split_reset

Clear the split count and index, disable split processing and clear STAT’s LYC interrupt-enable bit.

Syntax

c
void __scroll_split_reset();

Return value

No return value. The affected state and when it takes effect are described in this entry.

Conditions and limits

The shared table holds eight entries. Appending neither applies nor sorts them, and excess entries are ignored. Rebuild with reset→push→commit at a safe frame boundary and space events far enough apart for the handler to finish. Interrupt latency means the scheduled line and first affected pixel need not coincide. It does not erase table bytes, clear IE, or disable CPU interrupts.

Usage example

c
__scroll_split_reset();

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Split the screen into three scrolling bands with BG X=0→8→16. Three 24×16 rectangles appear at screen (32,16), (24,80) and (16,112). Events are scheduled at LY=64 and 104. Rectangles are black on DMG and red on CGB.

Complete example program

Build command

powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .\out | Out-Null
.\kitaqgb\kitaqgb.exe .\kitaq-docs\samples\api-examples\gb\batch2_split_intrinsics.c -I .\kitaqgb\lib -I .\kitaq-docs\samples -o .\out\batch2_split_intrinsics.gb --no-cache --no-disasm --profile=dev --rst-disable --stack-bank=fixed --cgb=cgb --cart=mbc5 --romsize=64k

                return;
            }

void AppendScrollHelpersIfUsed(List<Expr> rawLines)
    {
        bool needScrollHelpers = UseScrollSplitHelpers;
        if (!needScrollHelpers)
        {
            foreach (var e in rawLines)
            {
                string m;
                AsmOperand o;
                if (!e.Match(Tag.Asm, out m, out o) || o == null || !o.Base.HasValue) continue;
                string target = o.Base.Value;
                if (target == "__kq_scroll_split_reset_core" ||
                    target == "__kq_scroll_split_push_core" ||
                    target == "__kq_scroll_split_commit_core")
                {
                    needScrollHelpers = true;
                    break;
                }
            }
        }

        if (!needScrollHelpers) return;

        EnsureScrollState();

        var injected = new List<Expr>();
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Comment, "[KITAQGB] injected scroll split helpers"));

        // Reset the split count/index and disable STAT coincidence interrupts; existing table bytes are left in place.
        string resetDone = "__kq_scroll_split_reset_done";
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Function, "__kq_scroll_split_reset_core"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("XOR_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_MEM_A", ScrollSplitCountVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_MEM_A", ScrollSplitEnabledVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_MEM_A", ScrollSplitIndexVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_A_MEM", new AsmOperand(0x41, AddressMode.HighMem))); // STAT
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("AND_IMM", new AsmOperand(0xBF, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x41, AddressMode.HighMem)));
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Label, resetDone));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("RET"));

        // Append staged LY, SCX, SCY, WX, WY and masked flags; silently ignore entries beyond the eight-slot capacity.
        string pushHaveRoom = "__kq_scroll_split_push_have_room";
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Function, "__kq_scroll_split_push_core"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", ScrollSplitCountVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("CP_IMM", new AsmOperand(ScrollSplitMaxEntries, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("JR_C", new AsmOperand(pushHaveRoom, AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("RET"));
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Label, pushHaveRoom));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_E_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_D_IMM", new AsmOperand(0, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_L_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_H_IMM", new AsmOperand(0, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("ADD_HL_HL"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("ADD_HL_DE"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("ADD_HL_HL"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_DE_IMM", new AsmOperand(ScrollSplitTableAddr, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("ADD_HL_DE"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", ScrollSplitTmpLyVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDI_HL_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", ScrollSplitTmpScxVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDI_HL_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", ScrollSplitTmpScyVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDI_HL_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", ScrollSplitTmpWxVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDI_HL_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", ScrollSplitTmpWyVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDI_HL_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", ScrollSplitTmpFlagsVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("AND_IMM", new AsmOperand(ScrollSplitFlagMask, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDI_HL_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", ScrollSplitCountVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("INC_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_MEM_A", ScrollSplitCountVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("RET"));

        // Schedule entry A by programming LYC and STAT bit 6, or disable that bit when A is outside the current count.
        string schedDisable = "__kq_scroll_schedule_next_disable";
        string schedDisabled = "__kq_scroll_schedule_next_disabled";
        string schedHaveTarget = "__kq_scroll_schedule_next_have_target";
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Function, "__kq_scroll_schedule_next"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_B_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", ScrollSplitCountVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("CP_B"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("JR_C", new AsmOperand(schedDisable, AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("JR_Z", new AsmOperand(schedDisable, AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Label, schedHaveTarget));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_B"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_E_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_D_IMM", new AsmOperand(0, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_L_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_H_IMM", new AsmOperand(0, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("ADD_HL_HL"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("ADD_HL_DE"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("ADD_HL_HL"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_DE_IMM", new AsmOperand(ScrollSplitTableAddr, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("ADD_HL_DE"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_HL"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x45, AddressMode.HighMem))); // LYC
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_A_MEM", new AsmOperand(0x41, AddressMode.HighMem))); // STAT
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("OR_IMM", new AsmOperand(0x40, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x41, AddressMode.HighMem)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("RET"));
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Label, schedDisable));
        // Do not rewrite a disabled STAT source: on DMG even writing zero
        // can raise a fresh request and repeatedly re-enter the STAT handler.
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_A_MEM", new AsmOperand(0x41, AddressMode.HighMem)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("AND_IMM", new AsmOperand(0x40, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("JR_Z", new AsmOperand(schedDisabled, AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_A_MEM", new AsmOperand(0x41, AddressMode.HighMem))); // STAT
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("AND_IMM", new AsmOperand(0xBF, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x41, AddressMode.HighMem)));
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Label, schedDisabled));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("RET"));

        // Apply the fields selected by an entry's flags. Show follows hide when both are set; palette color zero reuses SCX/SCY bytes.
        string applySkipBg = "__kq_scroll_apply_entry_skip_bg";
        string applySkipWin = "__kq_scroll_apply_entry_skip_win";
        string applySkipHide = "__kq_scroll_apply_entry_skip_hide";
        string applySkipBgColor0 = "__kq_scroll_apply_entry_skip_bg_color0";
        string applyWaitPalette = "__kq_scroll_apply_entry_wait_palette";
        string applyDone = "__kq_scroll_apply_entry_done";
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Function, "__kq_scroll_apply_entry"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("INC_HL")); // scx
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_HL"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_B_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("INC_HL")); // scy
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_HL"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_C_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("INC_HL")); // wx
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_HL"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_D_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("INC_HL")); // wy
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_HL"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_E_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("INC_HL")); // flags
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_HL"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("AND_IMM", new AsmOperand(ScrollSplitFlagMask, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_H_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_H"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("AND_IMM", new AsmOperand(ScrollSplitFlagUseBg, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("JR_Z", new AsmOperand(applySkipBg, AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_B"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x43, AddressMode.HighMem))); // SCX
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_C"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x42, AddressMode.HighMem))); // SCY
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Label, applySkipBg));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_H"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("AND_IMM", new AsmOperand(ScrollSplitFlagUseWin, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("JR_Z", new AsmOperand(applySkipWin, AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_D"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x4B, AddressMode.HighMem))); // WX
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_E"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x4A, AddressMode.HighMem))); // WY
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Label, applySkipWin));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_H"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("AND_IMM", new AsmOperand(ScrollSplitFlagWinHide, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("JR_Z", new AsmOperand(applySkipHide, AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_A_MEM", new AsmOperand(0x40, AddressMode.HighMem))); // LCDC
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("AND_IMM", new AsmOperand(0xDF, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x40, AddressMode.HighMem)));
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Label, applySkipHide));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_H"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("AND_IMM", new AsmOperand(ScrollSplitFlagWinShow, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("JR_Z", new AsmOperand(applySkipBgColor0, AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_A_MEM", new AsmOperand(0x40, AddressMode.HighMem))); // LCDC
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("OR_IMM", new AsmOperand(0x20, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x40, AddressMode.HighMem)));
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Label, applySkipBgColor0));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_H"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("AND_IMM", new AsmOperand(ScrollSplitFlagBgColor0, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("JR_Z", new AsmOperand(applyDone, AddressMode.Absolute)));
        // CGB palette data writes are blocked during pixel transfer. Wait through
        // OAM search as well, so both color bytes fit in the following HBlank.
        // The LY-zero entry runs in VBlank and does not wait here.
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Label, applyWaitPalette));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_A_MEM", new AsmOperand(0x41, AddressMode.HighMem)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("AND_IMM", new AsmOperand(0x02, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("JR_NZ", new AsmOperand(applyWaitPalette, AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_IMM", new AsmOperand(0x80, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x68, AddressMode.HighMem))); // BCPS: palette 0, color 0, auto increment
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_B"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x69, AddressMode.HighMem))); // BCPD low
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_C"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x69, AddressMode.HighMem))); // BCPD high
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Label, applyDone));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("RET"));

        // Capture base window visibility and arm a nonempty table at index zero, enabling VBlank/STAT interrupts and issuing EI.
        string commitDisable = "__kq_scroll_split_commit_disable";
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Function, "__kq_scroll_split_commit_core"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_A_MEM", new AsmOperand(0x40, AddressMode.HighMem))); // LCDC
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("AND_IMM", new AsmOperand(0x20, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_MEM_A", ScrollWinVisibleVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", ScrollSplitCountVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("OR_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("JR_Z", new AsmOperand(commitDisable, AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_IMM", new AsmOperand(1, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_MEM_A", ScrollSplitEnabledVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("XOR_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_MEM_A", ScrollSplitIndexVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("CALL", new AsmOperand("__kq_scroll_schedule_next", AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", new AsmOperand(0xFFFF, AddressMode.Absolute))); // IE
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("OR_IMM", new AsmOperand(0x03, AddressMode.Immediate))); // VBlank | STAT
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0xFFFF, AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("EI"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("RET"));
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Label, commitDisable));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("XOR_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_MEM_A", ScrollSplitEnabledVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_MEM_A", ScrollSplitIndexVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("CALL", new AsmOperand("__kq_scroll_schedule_next", AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("RET"));

        // Save registers/SVBK, select WRAM bank 1, restore base scroll state and restart the split sequence for the frame.
        // A first entry at LY zero is applied immediately before scheduling the following entry.
        string vbDisable = "__kq_vblank_disable";
        string vbFirstNonZero = "__kq_vblank_first_nonzero";
        string vbDone = "__kq_vblank_done";
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Function, "__kq_vblank_vector"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("PUSH_AF"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("PUSH_BC"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("PUSH_DE"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("PUSH_HL"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_A_MEM", new AsmOperand(0x70, AddressMode.HighMem))); // SVBK
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("PUSH_AF"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_IMM", new AsmOperand(1, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x70, AddressMode.HighMem)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_IMM", new AsmOperand(1, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        // Set the existing fixed-address frame-ready flag used by the VBlank path.
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0xC29C, AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", ScrollBgXCurVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x43, AddressMode.HighMem))); // SCX
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", ScrollBgYCurVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x42, AddressMode.HighMem))); // SCY
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", ScrollWinXCurVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x4B, AddressMode.HighMem))); // WX
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", ScrollWinYCurVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x4A, AddressMode.HighMem))); // WY
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_A_MEM", new AsmOperand(0x40, AddressMode.HighMem))); // LCDC
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("AND_IMM", new AsmOperand(0xDF, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_B_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", ScrollWinVisibleVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("OR_B"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x40, AddressMode.HighMem)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", ScrollSplitEnabledVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("OR_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("JR_Z", new AsmOperand(vbDisable, AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", ScrollSplitCountVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("OR_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("JR_Z", new AsmOperand(vbDisable, AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("XOR_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_MEM_A", ScrollSplitIndexVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", new AsmOperand(ScrollSplitTableAddr, AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("OR_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("JR_NZ", new AsmOperand(vbFirstNonZero, AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_HL_IMM", new AsmOperand(ScrollSplitTableAddr, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("CALL", new AsmOperand("__kq_scroll_apply_entry", AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_IMM", new AsmOperand(1, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_MEM_A", ScrollSplitIndexVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("CALL", new AsmOperand("__kq_scroll_schedule_next", AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("JR", new AsmOperand(vbDone, AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Label, vbFirstNonZero));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("XOR_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("CALL", new AsmOperand("__kq_scroll_schedule_next", AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("JR", new AsmOperand(vbDone, AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Label, vbDisable));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("CALL", new AsmOperand("__kq_scroll_schedule_next", AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Label, vbDone));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("POP_AF"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x70, AddressMode.HighMem))); // restore SVBK
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("POP_HL"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("POP_DE"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("POP_BC"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("POP_AF"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("RETI"));

        // Save registers/SVBK, apply the current entry and advance its index, or disable further coincidence interrupts at the end.
        string statDisable = "__kq_stat_disable";
        string statDone = "__kq_stat_done";
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Function, "__kq_stat_vector"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("PUSH_AF"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("PUSH_BC"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("PUSH_DE"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("PUSH_HL"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_A_MEM", new AsmOperand(0x70, AddressMode.HighMem))); // SVBK
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("PUSH_AF"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_IMM", new AsmOperand(1, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x70, AddressMode.HighMem)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", ScrollSplitEnabledVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("OR_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("JR_Z", new AsmOperand(statDisable, AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", ScrollSplitIndexVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_B_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", ScrollSplitCountVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("CP_B"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("JR_C", new AsmOperand(statDisable, AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("JR_Z", new AsmOperand(statDisable, AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_B"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_E_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_D_IMM", new AsmOperand(0, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_L_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_H_IMM", new AsmOperand(0, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("ADD_HL_HL"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("ADD_HL_DE"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("ADD_HL_HL"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_DE_IMM", new AsmOperand(ScrollSplitTableAddr, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("ADD_HL_DE"));
        // DMG STAT writes can request an interrupt unrelated to LYC. Consume
        // this entry only on its scheduled line; leave the index intact otherwise.
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_HL"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_B_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_A_MEM", new AsmOperand(0x44, AddressMode.HighMem)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("CP_B"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("JR_NZ", new AsmOperand(statDone, AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("CALL", new AsmOperand("__kq_scroll_apply_entry", AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_A_MEM", ScrollSplitIndexVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("INC_A"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LD_MEM_A", ScrollSplitIndexVar));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("CALL", new AsmOperand("__kq_scroll_schedule_next", AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("JR", new AsmOperand(statDone, AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Label, statDisable));
        // Acknowledge an already-disabled source without writing STAT again.
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_A_MEM", new AsmOperand(0x41, AddressMode.HighMem)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("AND_IMM", new AsmOperand(0x40, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("JR_Z", new AsmOperand(statDone, AddressMode.Absolute)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_A_MEM", new AsmOperand(0x41, AddressMode.HighMem))); // STAT
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("AND_IMM", new AsmOperand(0xBF, AddressMode.Immediate)));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x41, AddressMode.HighMem)));
        injected.Add(Expr.Make(Tag.Label, statDone));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("POP_AF"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("LDH_MEM_A", new AsmOperand(0x70, AddressMode.HighMem))); // restore SVBK
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("POP_HL"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("POP_DE"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("POP_BC"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("POP_AF"));
        injected.Add(Expr.MakeAsm("RETI"));

        int insertAt = 0;
        while (insertAt < rawLines.Count && rawLines[insertAt].MatchTag(Tag.RstMap)) insertAt++;
        rawLines.InsertRange(insertAt, injected);
    }
__scroll_win_add

Add signed deltas to tracked window coordinates and apply them immediately.

Syntax

c
void __scroll_win_add(s8 dx, s8 dy);

Parameters

dx

Signed horizontal pixel delta, −128 through 127.

dy

Signed vertical pixel delta, −128 through 127.

Return value

No return value. The affected state and when it takes effect are described in this entry.

Conditions and limits

No wait is performed. Immediate setters/additions synchronize the affected pending pair to current values and clear its dirty flag. Even a single-axis immediate setter cancels the other pending axis in the same pair. Results wrap modulo 256. Additions start from tracked current values, not pending values or temporary raster register values.

Usage example

c
__scroll_win_add(4,-40);result[24]=M_WX;result[25]=M_WY;

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

Learn immediate versus pending values and wrapping signed additions. BG X is 250 before flush and 16 afterward; WX changes from 23 to 39. Adding −20 to BG X produces 252; adding −40 to WY produces 248. The visual example also shows a background rectangle and an independent window frame.

Complete example program

Build command

powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .\out | Out-Null
.\kitaqgb\kitaqgb.exe .\kitaq-docs\samples\api-examples\gb\batch2_scroll_intrinsics.c -I .\kitaqgb\lib -I .\kitaq-docs\samples -o .\out\batch2_scroll_intrinsics.gb --no-cache --no-disasm --profile=dev --rst-disable --stack-bank=fixed --cgb=cgb --cart=mbc5 --romsize=64k

Usage example

c
Camera_Init(&view);
Camera_Set(&view,2048,4096);
Camera_ApplyBg(&view);
Scroll_SetWindow(103,80);
Scroll_WindowShow();

This is a calling fragment. Follow the stated initialization and buffer requirements before using it in a complete program.

Expected result

With camera (8,16), the red 32×24 rectangle appears at screen (24,16). The window shows a blue 64×64 frame at (96,80) and a green 16×16 square at (112,96). All shapes are black on DMG.
